summary.headline: ASK Automotive Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 52.1% and EBITDA reached Rs. 164 crore (12% margin), with a record PAT of Rs. 85 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with consolidated revenue up 52.1% YoY (33.4% excluding alloy pass-through, and down 6.6% from the wheel assembly exit). EBITDA rose 32.7% YoY to Rs. 164 crore but the margin of 12% was diluted by the pass-through of a sharp aluminium alloy price spike. PAT grew 28.8% to Rs. 85 crore and EPS was Rs. 4.32 versus Rs. 3.35. Management raised FY27 growth guidance to high-teens from mid-teens and lifted the capex plan to about Rs. 700 crore from Rs. 450-500 crore, to be funded partly by term loans and higher working capital debt.

segments.name: Advanced braking system
segments.commentary: Revenue up 48% YoY in Q1; management says it sustains market leadership in this segment.

segments.name: Aluminium lightweighting precision solutions (alloy wheels)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 75% YoY in Q1; HPDC alloy wheel first supply started to a Japanese customer via Kyushu Yanagawa collaboration at Karoli. Wheel assembly revenue is nil from 1 April 2026 after strategic exit.

segments.name: Safety control cable
segments.commentary: Revenue up 20% YoY in Q1; sunroof cable initial supplies expected from H2 FY27, with substantial growth next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guidance revised to high-teens (previously mid-teens); management expects the Q1 momentum to continue through the year.
Capex for FY27 revised to about Rs. 700 crore from earlier Rs. 450-500 crore, driven by a new South India (Bangalore) plant targeted to be operational before March 2027.
Confirmed alloy wheel orders of Rs. 70-90 crore for FY27 depending on customer ramp-up, and Rs. 250 crore confirmed for FY28.
Ford export business expected at Rs. 40-45 crore in FY27, rising to about Rs. 60 crore in FY28.
Export growth guidance of 20% for FY27, which management says it remains confident of achieving.
Management expects EBITDA margin to recover to about 13.5-14% as aluminium prices cool, though conditional on geopolitics; aluminium has fallen more than 10% from peak of about Rs. 365.
AISIN JV expected to turn marginally profitable by end of Q1 FY28 quarter (not significant); revenue guidance for the JV to be given with Q4 call for FY28.
Debt-to-equity to remain below 0.5 per management; current debt levels to be disclosed with Q2 results.
capex_capacity: New South India plant in Bangalore (18th plant) to be operational before March 2027 to serve new orders.
Karoli plant utilisation rose to about 75% from 60-65% last quarter; management expects about 80% by Q4 FY27. Karoli has about 20% more land scope; Rs. 750 crore already invested there.
Captive solar: 9.9 MW Sirsa (Haryana) plant fully operational; 11.55 MW Bikaner (Rajasthan) plant ready, commissioning expected Q2 FY27. Payback 5-5.5 years.
Capex funding: internal accruals plus term loans for machines and working capital borrowing.
Workforce rose to over 9,000 from over 7,000 in February, with 500 more to be recruited soon at Karoli; management expects more than 10,000 next year.
demand_pricing: Industry: two-wheeler production 72.5 lakh units in Q1 FY27 vs 59.5 lakh, +22.8% YoY (per SIAM as cited); total vehicle production +22.1%.
Management attributes industry strength to GST 2.0 rate cut, income tax changes, RBI rate cuts, and a favourable base.
Alloy price pass-through is 100% back-to-back with customers and hedged, so absolute EBITDA is protected; margin % moves inversely with aluminium prices.
Management says no pass-through lag is pending; all alloy cost increases have been received from customers.
New orders are broad-based across ICE and EV, with EV substantial and concentrated in ALPS. One major EV customer has underperformed for some time, distorting EV growth.
Honda (largest customer) plans 10 new models; management says content per vehicle is highest for this customer.
Export negotiations ongoing with 2-3 players; a big export order to be announced only on materialisation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 33% revenue inflation is alloy pass-through in the braking division, and what are FY27/FY28 alloy wheel and Ford order sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management had not calculated the braking-division share; Kuldip Rathee estimated about 28% impact if prices rose about 48%. Confirmed alloy wheel orders are Rs. 70-90 crore for FY27 and Rs. 250 crore for FY28; Ford exports Rs. 40-45 crore in FY27 and about Rs. 60 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is a new South plant needed, and what are capex and utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: New orders from an existing customer require a Bangalore plant to be operational before March 2027. Capex guidance rose from Rs. 450-500 crore to about Rs. 700 crore; Karoli utilisation is about 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AISIN JV still loss-making and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramping up with more products; profitability expected by end of the current quarter, but not significant as it is mainly trading. Revenue guidance for FY28 to come with the Q4 call.

qa_highlights.question: Is any commodity pass-through still pending with a lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No lag pending; customers have passed through everything. Absolute EBITDA is unaffected; only percentage margin moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.7% adjusted margin (analyst's calculation) sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst's math was described as nearly right, but management said 15% is not sustainable; overall margin expected at about 13.5-14%.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and how has debt moved?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals plus term loans for machines; debt rose in Q1 due to working capital needs from higher aluminium prices. Debt-to-equity to stay below 0.5; exact debt to be disclosed in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EV growth in two-wheelers similar to ICE, given faster EV industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: ASK is growing in EV with all top customers, but one major EV customer with large revenue has underperformed for some time, distorting the percentage.

financial_highlights.value: 52.1% YoY (33.4% ex alloy pass-through; net of 6.6% wheel assembly reduction, +25.3%)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs. 33 crore in Q1 FY26

risks_watch: Aluminium price path and geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict, Hormuz): management says the 13.5-14% EBITDA margin should come but depends on geopolitics; a renewed block could keep margins near 12%.
Capex rise from Rs. 450-500 crore to about Rs. 700 crore plus higher working capital debt; debt-to-equity guided below 0.5 but current debt figure not disclosed until Q2 results.

Concentration and execution: Honda is the largest customer; one major EV customer has underperformed for some time; alloy wheel Taiwanese partner approval still under testing; sunroof cable supplies start H2 FY27.

Confirmed FY27 alloy wheel orders of Rs. 70-90 crore depend on customer ramp-up; Ford export business Rs. 40-45 crore in FY27; export growth target 20% for FY27 with no big export order announced yet.

Bangalore plant must be operational before March 2027 and Karoli utilisation target of about 80% by Q4 FY27; AISIN JV still loss-making with revenue guidance deferred to the Q4 call for FY28; ABS mandate still a draft with no final decision.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident and assertive on volumes, guidance (raised to high-teens) and order wins, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, citing geopolitics, and deferred several numbers (braking-division alloy impact, current debt, JV revenue, captive solar savings) to later disclosures.
